newsitem.title: USA: Plan to boost Pacific Intertie capacity delayed.
newsitem.headline: Plan to boost Pacific Intertie capacity delayed.

text.p: A Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) study group has decided to conduct further studies before considering a proposal to raise capacity on the Pacific Intertie power lines this spring, a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) spokesman said Thursday.
The group decided to study whether direct loads in southern California should be tripped off if conditions such as those which caused widespread power blackouts last summer happen again, he said.
The Intertie lines, which link the Pacific Northwest to California, have been capped at 5,200 MW since last summer, compared with a capacity of 7,900 MW.
A plan to raise the limit to 6,250 MW was approved by the WSCC board last week and general members of the reliability council are currently reviewing it.
If supported by WSCC members, the "winter" increase on the intertie is expected to go into effect Saturday, BPA said.
The WSCC study group will meet again April 9 to review the "spring" plan which calls for raising the limit as high as 7,800 MW.
But BPA is not confident of the capacity being raised that high and is very concerned about the length of the WSCC review, the spokesman said.
Under the schedule put forward this week, the study group would finalize a report on the spring rate by April 20, with the WSCC board to vote on it April 24.

But concerns have been raised that operating conditions on the Northwest hydroelectric system will have changed so much by then--mainly lower regional loads and higher generation--that criteria for the winter plan would be obsolete by the time the spring plan is approved.
If that were to happen, the Intertie capacity would revert to 5,200 MW until the spring plan is implemented.
